title: The Basque demand for a separate country
body: Basque is a hilly and prosperous region of Spain that the Spanish government recognises as an autonomous region within the Spanish federation. Leaders of the Basque Nationalist Movement are not satisfied with this autonomy and want the region to become a separate country; supporters have used constitutional and, till recently, violent means. They argue that Basque culture is very different from Spanish culture, that the Basque language does not resemble Spanish (though only about one-third of the people understand it today), and that the hilly terrain makes the region geographically distinct. Since Roman times the region had its own arrangements for justice, administration and finance. The modern movement began near the end of the nineteenth century when Spanish rulers tried to abolish these arrangements; later the dictator Franco cut autonomy further and banned the Basque language even in homes. These measures have since been withdrawn, but movement leaders remain suspicious of the Spanish government and fearful of 'outsiders'. Opponents say the separatists seek political gains from an issue already resolved.
